all_reforms_including_excluded.description: The Employment Adjustment Grant scheme, effective from January 1975, provided financial support to temporarily laid-off workers, with public funds covering a significant portion of the allowance for large and small enterprises.
all_reforms_including_excluded.growth_orientation_rationale: By providing financial support to laid-off workers, the scheme helps maintain workforce stability and promotes occupational mobility, which can enhance overall productivity.
all_reforms_including_excluded.status_evidence: The scheme has been effective since January 1975.
all_reforms_including_excluded.importance_rationale: The scheme represents a significant intervention in the labor market, aimed at stabilizing employment during economic fluctuations, thus having a meaningful impact on human capital.
all_reforms_including_excluded.source_quote: Under this scheme, effective as from January 1975, of the allowance paid to temporarily laid-off workers, half was financed by public funds in the case of large enterprises and two-thirds in the case of small and medium-sized ones.
all_reforms_including_excluded.cross_verification_note: The description focuses on financial support for temporarily laid-off workers, which does not directly relate to R&D funding or knowledge transfer mechanisms.
